package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised via a supply chain attack in which attackers injected malicious code into the legitimate software update process. This code created a backdoor (SUNBURST/Solorigate) that enabled remote access and control over affected systems, impacting approximately 18,000 downstream customers, including critical US government agencies.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (trojanized DLL within Orion update package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a covert network connection to a remote command-and-control (C2) server (avsvmcloud.com), awaits instructions, and executes received commands, enabling remote access and control over the compromised system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces unauthorized remote access capabilities by contacting an external C2 server and executing arbitrary commands, which is not expected in legitimate network management software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Orion DLLs should not contain logic to beacon to external servers or execute remote commands. The presence of such behavior is a clear violation of expected software functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may contact update servers or telemetry endpoints, but not arbitrary external C2 infrastructure or execute remote code without user consent.
key_indicators: Execution of remote commands from external source
Code hidden within a legitimate DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll)

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious code into the SolarWinds Orion build process, trojanizing a core DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in official SolarWinds Orion software updates.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised Orion update, deploying the trojanized DLL to their systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now present and able to execute on customer systems.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, the malicious DLL initiates a covert connection to the attacker's C2 server and awaits further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access and can execute arbitrary commands on victim systems.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion processes to avsvmcloud.com or similar C2 domains
Orion DLLs or processes executing arbitrary code or commands received from the network
Presence of previously unseen or modified DLLs in the Orion installation directory
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (with hash not matching official release)
Unexpected modifications to Orion platform DLLs
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Unusual HTTP/S traffic from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion platform installations for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Check the integrity of core Orion DLLs against official hashes. Alert on any Orion process executing code or commands received from the network. Use EDR and network monitoring to detect suspicious process behaviors and network traffic patterns.
